narrator.note: Documentary/textbook register, same brief as the Russian track's narrator: explains, never dramatizes.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Last time, this came from software. It also comes from somewhere else.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Every company can be drawn as a set of functions - the jobs it has to do to create value.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: These are the functions that build the product and get it to a customer - the primary work.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Underneath, the functions that make the first row possible, without building the product themselves.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: What's left over, once both rows have done their work - the difference between what it cost and what it earned.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: This is a value chain. It says what a company does. It does not yet say how the work actually moves.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That gap is exactly where this chapter is headed.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Say this box is where the actual work happens. What does work look like, up close?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Break work into small, specialized pieces - one worker, one narrow task each. This is Taylorism. It built the industrial revolution.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: On a factory floor, that worked. Each step was simple. A worker didn't need to know what happened before - just do the one thing in front of them.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Modern work doesn't stay this simple. Each step here needs to know the whole case, not just its own task.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Every handoff, someone has to reconstruct the context from nothing. That reconstruction - not the task itself - is what actually costs time.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Combine the small steps back into fewer, wider ones -

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: - and give them to people who understand the whole case, not just one narrow piece of it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Zoom back out. A company doesn't run on one function. It runs on a handful of processes - and each one stays a closed box.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: None of these are opened up. What matters here is only what crosses the line between them.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: This is as deep as the org level goes - a name, a manager, what comes in, what goes out. Not a flowchart of how the work happens inside.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Open it further, and you're no longer describing the company - you're describing one process's own internal work. Different question, different level.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: What happens at these lines is, more than almost anything inside the boxes, what the business is actually judged on.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A shape for what the company does. A reason the work has to be grouped coarser than Taylor would have grouped it. And a boundary around each process that stays deliberately closed.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Different road than last time. Same destination.
